engine.source: vertex_engine.stations, vertex_magnet (NOMINAL coil set, exact loop fields), vertex_radiation.implied_target

startup.source: lab/studies/ignition-failures results (constants, reference); vertex_magnet stored energy

steps.title: Electrical power to the engine bay
steps.text: The cluster takes power through its power bay. Which source carries the driver is not budgeted: the only budgeted store is the 720 MJ pulse bank, charged at 50 MW.

steps.title: Coils cold
steps.text: The superconducting windings are held near 20 K by the cryogenic circuit before any current flows. A warm spot in a winding would end superconductivity there.

steps.title: Current ramps up in the coils
steps.text: Six coils per engine take -5.4 to 11.6 mega-ampere-turns. The field stores 9.7 GJ per engine. At an illustrative 100 MW the ramp takes 97 s.

steps.title: The magnetic nozzle forms
steps.text: The field lines form a closed cusp ahead of the burn point and open aft into the nozzle. 1.46 T at the burn point (vacuum field: no plasma yet, and a field alone makes no plasma and no fusion).

steps.title: Readiness checks
steps.text: Field map, coil temperatures, quench detection, bore shutter, target magazine and driver alignment. The quench protection must absorb 9.7 GJ if a coil goes normal; no dump system is sized yet.

steps.title: Driver power for the targets
steps.text: At the mission rate the target drivers need 1.43 TW (gain 100, 50 % efficient): 28,630 times the pulse bank's power. This is the first thing that fails, after 0.50 ms.

fuel.h2_note: The hydrogen flow is the mission state (operating_point); divided by the design pulse rate it mixes two states and is shown only for scale. How MeV fusion products give their energy to cold hydrogen is SPECULATIVE and belongs to the engine workstream; the hydrogen opens only after ignition (FPS states IGNITION, then PROPELLANT FEED).

nuclear.source: Coulomb barrier at touching radii (R = 1.2 A^1/3 fm), Gamow energy, Bosch-Hale 1992 cross-section fit; momentum-transfer Coulomb cross section 8 ln(Lambda) x pi b90^2 with ln(Lambda) = 20

dt_ref.note: D-T, for scale: about 1.5e20 m^-3 s near 25 keV (textbook ignition)

burn.open: How the target reaches its areal density (the driver and the implosion) is not modelled anywhere in the project: the burn starts from an assumed compressed, heated sphere.

nozzle.source: Boris push in the NOMINAL vacuum field (vertex_magnet.field3, hardware, obstacle); field x4 scales every coil current; no plasma response, no collisions, so detachment is not shown

channels.source: lab/studies/fusion-ignition/imports/compact_aebbb0d.json (lab/studies/vertex-compact-engine/vertex-compact compact.py, quick run, 48 directions x 4 species)

C2.label: C2 cluster 30 m aft on a longer thrust truss

C3.label: C3 C2 + 6 m spool (burn 12 m aft of the shield), ribbon loops, tank-shadowing shields

C4.label: C4 C3 + braking protection package (15 m screen zone)

polarised.label: D and 3He spins aligned: D-3He rate x1.5

polarised-dd.label: Aligned, and D-D assumed suppressed x0.25

field.note: The closure field times 1, 2 or 4. In the drawn cluster (C1) more field changes almost nothing: the products that miss the nozzle hit the shield and loops before the field turns them. In C3 the burn sits farther from the shield, which helps more.

armour.source: MPN rule used in lab/studies/vertex-compact-engine/vertex-compact/problems.py: W-B4C attenuation length 0.08 m, scattered floor 1e-4
armour.note: Thicker armour helps until the neutrons scattered round it dominate; that floor alone is about 11 times the winding limit.

mirrors.source: Thermal bremsstrahlung spectrum at Te; supermirror cut-off K / theta with K = 16 keV deg and R = 0.5 (order of hard X-ray telescope optics); neutrons and charged products are not reflected
mirrors.note: A mirror only helps where the photons meet it at a grazing angle. To intercept the same share of the sky at angle theta, a surface must be about 1 / sin(theta) times longer, and half the photons it accepts are still absorbed in it. On the drawn engine the faces meet the rays at a median 54 deg, where a coating returns 1.5e-05 of what strikes (thermal study, strategy A): this lever asks what if the faces were grazing.

spin.note: Polarised D and 3He: D-3He rate up to x1.5 in theory, never shown in a burning plasma. The D-D suppression option is SPECULATIVE.

variants.note: C1 is the approved cluster; C2-C4 move it 30-36 m aft and are research, not canon. C4 is the recommended compact research direction, not a validated design.

items.title: Compact engine hardware absorbs most of the burn
items.mechanism: Loops, shield and closure coils within 2-12 m of a 65 TW burn see most of its sky and take 46-69 % of the charged products
items.required: Piped heat <= 10.8 GW (four engines, the canon drive radiators)
items.solutions: Stronger closure field (x4 already used in C3), ribbon loops, larger loop radii within the cluster envelope, lower-loss fuel cycle
items.advances: Absorbed fraction 4e-5 of fusion power (today about 0.45); a field that keeps charged products off hardware at 2-10 m
items.next: Hybrid PIC of the compact burn with C1-C2 closure coils at x4 field
items.assumptions: V2 optimistic fuel (1.6B S5), vacuum test particles, ron.py sky ledger

items.title: Compact axial efficiency 0.31-0.51 inflates the mass ratio
items.mechanism: Products hitting the shield and leaving radially do not make thrust; ve falls with eta
items.required: eta about 0.95 (canon ve)
items.achieved: C1 0.31, C3 0.51; departure 48,744 t even if the heat closed
items.solutions: Field x4 and burn 12 m aft of the shield (C3) raise eta 0.31 to 0.51
items.next: Full 160-direction run; scan field x2-x8
items.assumptions: Test particles, 48 directions x 4 species (quick run)

items.title: Burns light the radiator blades and the aft ship
items.mechanism: Shadow cones of the drawn shields (28 deg) do not cover the spine, the tank dome or the blade roots beside the cluster
items.required: <= 0.1 GW direct burn on the ship
items.achieved: C1 1,255 GW; C2 76 GW (cluster 30 m aft); C4 13.9 GW, all on the blade aft ends
items.solutions: Cluster 30 m aft (16x less), tank-shadowing shields (C3/C4), move the blade aft station forward or cant the blade aft ends edge-on
items.advances: None for C4: a geometry change of the blade aft station (PROTOTYPE) closes most of the remainder
items.next: Blade aft-station trade (area kept)
items.assumptions: No ship self-occlusion; photons + neutrons; four canted burns

items.title: Loop windings take 7,000 x their neutron fluence limit
items.mechanism: Windings 7.6 m from the burn behind 0.22 m of armour (drawn)
items.solutions: No armour thickness closes: the scattered floor alone is 11 x the limit. Replaceable loop cassettes (one set per burn, about 11 exchanges per mission), or a winding farther from the burn
items.advances: Radiation-tolerant conductor at 34e22 n/m2 with thicker armour; or neutron-lean fuel
items.next: Neutron transport for the compact loop armour
items.assumptions: W-B4C attenuation 0.08 m, scattered floor 1e-4 (MPN rule)

items.title: Engine faces lead in braking: armour only
items.mechanism: Loops, shield faces and the hub lead into the dust in braking; nothing can stand ahead of them in the burn view
items.required: 0.1 breaches per face
items.achieved: Armour 8-10 cm W/C: 444 t NOMINAL, 780 t JUSTIFIED (whole aft end)
items.solutions: Replaceable armour tiles on the loop aft faces and the hub cap (C4)
items.next: Tile layout on the loop cryostats
items.assumptions: Dust-impacts rules, extrapolated above 100 km/s

items.title: Compact stern screens close for the tank dome (NOMINAL)
items.mechanism: Three screens in a 15 m zone ahead of the tank dome, inside the enlarged shields' shadow
items.required: 0.1 events
items.achieved: 0.086 events NOMINAL with 5.5 t; JUSTIFIED needs more stand-off
items.solutions: Screens become roll-fed spares; armour remains the JUSTIFIED answer
items.next: JUSTIFIED screen count vs shield size
items.assumptions: HIMS-B pass-through 0.5 per screen (NOMINAL)

items.title: Hull-shadowing shields grow and add engine heat
items.mechanism: Shadowing the tank dome from a burn 24 m off axis needs a 40-46 deg shield; it adds sky (heat) and mass
items.required: Shadow the ship without extra heat
items.achieved: C3 shield r 7.9 m (375 t/engine); C4 r 9.5 m (533 t/engine)
items.solutions: One cluster-wide shadow disc on the hub instead of four large cones (to study)
items.next: Cluster shadow-disc variant
items.assumptions: LiH body, 5 cm W/B4C face

items.title: Longer thrust truss and feeds (30-36 m)
items.mechanism: Cluster moved aft on twelve truss members; feeds, trunks and the Li/cold loops lengthen
items.required: Carries 21.8 MN and the field loads
items.achieved: Drawn, not sized (30 t per engine allotted)
items.solutions: Size with vertex_structure loads
items.next: Truss FE with the cluster load cases
items.assumptions: PROTOTYPE

items.title: Ripple heating of the compact eddy shields
items.mechanism: 5.7 kHz pulses (AMPN rule, eps_c 0.3)
items.required: Radiated by the shield at <= 2,300 K
items.achieved: 41 MW per engine, dB/B 0.001
items.solutions: Booked in the piped heat
items.next: With ENG-002
items.assumptions: Coupling 0.3 (0.1-1) not measured

items.title: Supermirrors meet the burn at the wrong angle
items.mechanism: X-ray mirrors reflect only at grazing angles of a few mrad; the burn-facing faces of the compact engine meet its rays at a median 54 deg
items.required: Reflected share of the X-rays on hardware that matters for heat (at least 0.5)
items.achieved: 1.5e-05 of the X-rays that strike (46 MW of 3.05 TW)
items.solutions: Edge-on structure (B) instead of coated faces; mirrors only where a surface can be made to contain the burn point
items.advances: None for hard X-rays: the critical angle is a property of matter (about 1/E)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: No grazing deflector can steer the spectrum clear of a coil
items.mechanism: Clearing a coil needs a turn of about its angular width (0.09-0.26 rad); a grazing mirror turns a ray by at most twice the critical angle (Pt 68 mrad at 1 keV)
items.required: A deflection of 0.1-0.26 rad inside the 11.5 m engine envelope
items.achieved: Only photons below about 0.1 keV; none in the R2-B spectrum (1-1000 keV)
items.solutions: Remote geometry (MPN candidate F, RON B) where coils subtend milliradians
items.advances: Not reachable with reflection; geometry only
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Mirror coatings do not survive the pulse
items.mechanism: Each pulse puts up to 3.4 MJ/m2 of X-rays on the armour in about 10 ps; a 0.5 nm mirror finish ablates on the first pulse; neutron and helium damage roughen it further
items.required: Roughness below 1 nm for 10^7 pulses per hour
items.achieved: Ablation every pulse (tungsten surface jump about 10^5 K)
items.solutions: None for a mirror face; sacrificial low-Z faces renewed in service
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Armour shoes cover only part of each coil
items.mechanism: The drawn shoes (0.22 m section) shadow 37% of the cryostat silhouette the burn sees; the rest strikes the bare vessel
items.required: Full silhouette armour
items.achieved: 1.80 TW on bare cryostat vessels and joints (no coolant drawn there)
items.solutions: Strategy C layered blankets (2,147 t per engine with neutron layers, 248 t without)
items.advances: Lighter neutron shielding (hydrides, boron carbide composites)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: No face material survives the X-ray pulse at 1800 K
items.mechanism: The pulse is far shorter than conduction: the surface layer takes the X-rays at once
items.required: Surface below melting or sublimation
items.achieved: Best is carbon: jump 2,866 K, margin -766 K; tungsten jumps 1.7e+05 K; Be and LiH survive the pulse but melt below the 1800 K loop
items.solutions: Low-Z sacrificial faces (carbon) at a colder loop; larger standoff (fluence falls as 1/d^2)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Heat flux far above any coolant channel
items.mechanism: Lithium-cooled tungsten carries about 20 MW/m2 steady
items.required: Below 20 MW/m2 on every hot face
items.achieved: 96-1,250 times the limit; the armour channels would need lithium at 7-28 km/s
items.solutions: Spread the heat (standoff, larger faces); reduce the engine's sky share
items.advances: None in the channel: the flux is set by geometry
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Drawn lithium lines are far too small
items.mechanism: The supply feeder (r 0.11 m) and panel lines (r 0.12 m) carry lithium at most 10 m/s with a 300 K rise
items.required: 5.82 TW (all engine heat); 2.7 GW even at the canon radiator share
items.achieved: 216 MW: 27,013 times short; the budget alone needs 0.48 m2 of flow area
items.solutions: Lines sized for the budget (several 0.2-0.3 m mains); the full heat would need a 18 m pipe
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Liquid-metal MHD pressure loss in the coil field
items.mechanism: Lithium crossing 1-2.4 T near the windings induces currents that drag the flow (dp ~ sigma v B^2 L c)
items.required: Below the 1 MPa design pressure
items.achieved: 2.2-48 MPa per armour run at 10 m/s with bare walls; 0.09-2.0 MPa with SiC inserts
items.solutions: SiC flow-channel inserts; runs along the field; helium or molten salt in the strongest field
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Cryogenic refrigeration demand
items.mechanism: Neutrons reach the 20 K windings through the bare vessels; each watt there costs 297 W of refrigerator input
items.required: Refrigeration within the engine's power budget (MW class)
items.achieved: 25.2 GW at 20 K -> 7.46 TW of input; with blankets C 1.3 GW -> 394.4 GW
items.solutions: Thick neutron shields on every coil; warmer superconductors (40-77 K REBCO)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Hot radiator area and mass
items.mechanism: Everything absorbed leaves by radiation at 1800 K
items.required: 2.7 GW per engine (canon share)
items.achieved: 1.09e+07 m2 per engine (404 times the ship's radiators, about 109 kt); Brayton recovery raises it 10-fold
items.solutions: Cut absorbed heat first; recovery runs the driver but enlarges the radiator
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Thermal fatigue at the pulse rate
items.mechanism: Every face is heated and relaxed at the pulse rate
items.required: Fatigue life of a renewable face over one service interval
items.achieved: 2.1e+07 cycles per hour; one burn of days is 10^9-10^10 cycles
items.solutions: Faces renewed between burns (exchange units)
items.advances: OPEN: no fatigue data at these cycle counts
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Hot and cryogenic circuits share a narrow gap
items.mechanism: The 1800 K armour shoe sits 0.16 m from the cryostat; radiation across the gap and the vessels' own heat need a warm stage
items.required: Separate hot, warm and cold circuits with no shared wall
items.achieved: 3.55 TW lands on warm parts drawn without a coolant; gap radiation about 4.1 MW per engine
items.solutions: A third (warm, about 300-600 K) circuit for vessels, cage and optics; polished screens in the gap
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Edge-on structure needs sub-milliradian alignment
items.mechanism: A blade works only while its plane contains the burn point to about 0.11 mrad (source wander over distance); thermal growth and coil forces move the cage by millimetres
items.required: Alignment held to 0.1-1 mrad through each burn
items.achieved: Budget 0.13 mrad (target miss, mount, 1 K thermal bow, vibration); a 3.3 K face-to-face difference alone uses the whole allowance; first mode 35 Hz against 5,697 Hz pulses
items.solutions: Both faces cooled together, active root trim from the edge temperature map, constrained-layer dampers, cones instead of flat hoops
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Driver final optics see the burn
items.mechanism: The six final-focus optics sit in the shield face with a direct view of the burn
items.required: Optics behind a shutter or a grazing turning mirror
items.achieved: 31.4 GW on 1.9 m2 of optics
items.solutions: Grazing metal turning mirrors (the one place a grazing mirror fits), fast shutters
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Protection mass exceeds the engine
items.mechanism: Full-silhouette blankets with neutron layers weigh about 3 t/m2
items.required: Protection mass a small share of the 1,242 t drawn engine
items.achieved: 2,147 t per engine (B+C 2,208 t)
items.solutions: Thin blankets (no neutron layers, about 250 t) with warmer windings
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Lithium leak or loss of flow in a magnet
items.mechanism: Lithium runs beside the cryostats; a leak shorts or attacks the vessel, a loss of flow lets the faces melt within milliseconds
items.required: Detection and isolation faster than the face heats
items.achieved: OPEN: no failure analysis
items.solutions: Double-walled runs, segment isolation valves, burn abort
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Engine pickup undercounted in the ledger
items.mechanism: The compact sky ledger counted coils, shield and loops; the cage hoops, seats, struts and lines also see the burn
items.required: One sky trace for every drawn part
items.achieved: Trace 63.1% vs the compact study's piped share 54.6% (x1.16)
items.solutions: Audited 2026-11-24: the 54.6 % was a piped-heat residual from the steady source, not a geometric share; the coupled ledger now uses the trace
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Edge-on blades concentrate the heat on their edges
items.mechanism: A blade aligned with the burn shows it only its edge, so the edge takes the full X-ray flux at its distance
items.required: Edge flux below the 20 MW/m2 a lithium-cooled face can take
items.achieved: 7.4 GW/m2 steady (372x), 1,102 K per pulse, 63% of CFC strength each pulse
items.solutions: Sacrificial replaceable edge strips on lithium-cooled roots (drawn), exchange ports at the aft hoop (drawn)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Blade alignment needs active trim
items.mechanism: Thermal bow of a 1 m blade by a few kelvin across its faces swings its plane off the burn point by more than the allowance
items.required: Plane held within 0.11 mrad
items.achieved: 3.3 K face difference allowed; actuators 6 t per engine (PROTOTYPE)
items.solutions: Root actuators with an AI controller reading the edge temperature map between pulses (drawn)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: The thin blanket does not cut the cryogenic load
items.mechanism: Without the W/B4C and LiH layers the neutrons reach the windings
items.required: 20 K load near the refrigeration a ship can carry
items.achieved: 25.2 GW at 20 K with the thin blanket (248 t); the archived full blanket reached 1.3 GW for 2,147 t
items.solutions: Warmer superconductors (fewer watts per watt), shadow shields at the source
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: The warm circuit needs a large radiator of its own
items.mechanism: An 850 K radiator rejects about a twentieth of the heat per square metre of the hot radiator
items.required: Warm load small enough for the ship WARM zone
items.solutions: Move blade-root heat into the hot loop; keep the warm loop for housings only
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: The target is its own X-ray lamp
items.mechanism: At the design density the 14.7 MeV protons stop within microns and give about 90 % of their energy to electrons, which radiate
items.required: X-ray share low enough that cooling can follow
items.achieved: 85% of the fusion energy as X-rays; hot ions, polarisation and 3He-rich fuel barely change it
items.solutions: Lower areal density, earlier extraction of the protons, an X-ray trapping tamper
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Energy taken from the X-rays strikes the nozzle instead
items.mechanism: Every lever that keeps energy in the plasma feeds the nozzle, and the compact nozzle puts about two thirds of the plasma on hardware
items.required: Hit share well below 0.1
items.achieved: Best source case: X-rays 23%, thrust x2.1, engine heat still x2,011 its radiator share (78% from strikes)
items.solutions: A nozzle with a small hit share (C3/C4 field, remote geometry)
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

items.title: Exhaust too slow for the mission
items.mechanism: The coupled pulse leaves too little directed energy per kilogram
items.required: 19,201 km/s (the mission exhaust speed)
items.achieved: 4,914 km/s coupled; 9,928 km/s with every source lever and a tamper
items.solutions: More directed energy per kilogram: early proton extraction, smaller hit share; never more cold propellant
items.next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)
items.assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

thermal.state_note: The COUPLED pulse of the Fusion Ignition ledger (R2-B design target at the design rate, C1 nozzle shares).

reconcile.note: This trace of every drawn part finds the hardware covering 63.1% of the burn's sky. The compact study's piped share (54.6%) is not a geometric figure: it is its piped heat minus the charged strikes, over the steady-plasma neutral power, and it leaves out the cage hoops, seats, struts and lines and what edge-on parts re-radiate. Since the 2026-11-24 audit (lab/studies/vertex-compact-engine/vertex-source) the coupled ledger uses this trace for its X-ray and neutron pickup.

pulsed.note: Surface temperature jump of one pulse at the hottest armour point (fluence per pulse times the spectrum-weighted absorption at the surface, over the volumetric heat capacity; the pulse is far shorter than heat conduction). C_diamond stands for carbon (CFC density). A low-Z face spreads the same X-rays over centimetres; tungsten takes them in the first micrometres.

brayton.note: Recovered electricity can run the driver, whose heat is already the ledger's heat_in: it replaces external power and adds no energy or thrust. The rest leaves at the cold side, so the radiator grows.

quench.note: Stored field energy of the engine coil set (NOMINAL); dumped into warm resistor banks on the pulse pods over the dump time, never into the hot lithium loop.

cryo.separation: The cryogenic circuit (20 K windings, 80 K screens, cold supports, leads, quench lines) shares no fluid, header or wall with the lithium circuit; the only coupling is radiation across the vacuum gap and conduction through the cold-mass supports.

A.title: Coated coil and shield faces (grazing X-ray and far-IR mirrors)
A.surfaces: Burn-facing armour shoes, LiH noses, shield burn face, bare cryostat areas
A.why: The faces meet the burn's rays at a median grazing angle of 54 deg; X-ray mirrors reflect only below a few mrad, so a coating returns 1.5e-05 of the X-rays that strike. In the STEADY regime a metal face already reflects 98.3% of far-IR synchrotron light; the coating adds nothing over a tungsten face, and helps only where the face would be B4C.

B.title: Edge-on structure: source-aligned blades and cones for the cage, seats, struts and lines
B.verdict: HELPS: LARGEST CUT, FAR FROM ENOUGH
B.why: A blade whose plane contains the burn point shows the burn only its 30 mm edge; its faces meet the rays at the source wander over distance (about 0.11 mrad), where a polished face reflects 99% of the spectrum. The members' heat falls to 8.9%; the hoops and the reaction ring become cones with their apex at the burn point. The photons that pass the blades go on to space or to the neighbour engines; nothing is stored.

blade.material: CFC with a replaceable tungsten-carbon edge strip (PROTOTYPE)

budget.term: Target miss at the burn point

budget.source: alpha dT / t over the span

alignment.note: The blade must hold its plane on the burn point to about 0.11 mrad. Thermal bow dominates: a face-to-face difference of only 3.33 K bends a 1.0 m blade that far, so both faces are cooled together and an active root actuator (sensed by the engine controller from the edge temperature map) trims the plane between pulses.

vibration.note: The first bending mode (35 Hz) is far below the 5,697 Hz pulse rate, so each pulse is a quasi-static load on the low modes; the risk is the dense high-order modes near the pulse rate and its harmonics, which need damping in the root joint (PROTOTYPE: constrained-layer dampers at every root).

edge.note: Edge-on concentrates what is left on the edge: 7.4 GW/m2 steady, 372 times a lithium-cooled face can take, and a 1,102 K jump each pulse. The edge is a sacrificial, replaceable strip on lithium-cooled roots.

integration.note: Blades bolt to the cage hoops, which become cones with their apex at the burn point; every blade root carries a lithium manifold tap, an actuator and a damper; edge strips change on the service rail.

D.title: Integrated grazing photonics in the nozzle (deflector collars, source-pointing liners)
D.liner_far_ir: Metal bore liners return far-IR synchrotron light in the STEADY regime (as A); in the coupled target pulse the synchrotron share is not modelled (OPEN).
D.why: To steer a ray clear of a coil, a grazing mirror must turn it by about the coil's angular width (0.1-0.2 rad here); X-ray mirrors turn rays by at most twice the critical angle (Pt: 68 mrad at 1 keV, falling as 1/E), which never reaches it inside the R2-B spectrum. No deflector inside the engine envelope removes measurable heat.

comparison.title: Drawn engine, no mirrors
comparison.why: Heat on this engine at the coupled pulse.

comparison.title: Coated coil and shield faces (grazing X-ray and far-IR mirrors)
comparison.acts: X-rays at grazing angles below a few mrad; far-IR (steady regime)
comparison.why: The faces meet the burn's rays at a median grazing angle of 54 deg; X-ray mirrors reflect only below a few mrad, so a coating returns 1.5e-05 of the X-rays that strike. In the STEADY regime a metal face already reflects 98.3% of far-IR synchrotron light; the coating adds nothing over a tungsten face, and helps only where the face would be B4C.

comparison.title: Edge-on structure: source-aligned blades and cones for the cage, seats, struts and lines
comparison.verdict: HELPS: LARGEST CUT, FAR FROM ENOUGH
comparison.why: A blade whose plane contains the burn point shows the burn only its 30 mm edge; its faces meet the rays at the source wander over distance (about 0.11 mrad), where a polished face reflects 99% of the spectrum. The members' heat falls to 8.9%; the hoops and the reaction ring become cones with their apex at the burn point. The photons that pass the blades go on to space or to the neighbour engines; nothing is stored.

comparison.acts: X-rays, neutrons and strikes on the coils
comparison.why: Absorbs instead of reflecting. It covers the cryostat silhouette the drawn shoes leave bare and cuts the neutron heat in the windings, so the cryogenic load falls; every joule it stops still goes into the lithium loop, so the hot load does not fall.

comparison.acts: X-rays and strikes on the bare cryostats
comparison.why: Without the W/B4C and LiH layers: the X-rays and strikes on the bare cryostats go to lithium, but the neutrons still reach the windings. It cools the bare cryostat walls (1.79 TW into lithium instead of into uncooled parts), but the 20 K load stays at 25.2 GW because the neutrons pass (the full blanket: 1.3 GW).

comparison.title: Edge-on structure and the thin blanket (current direction)
comparison.why: The owner's current direction (2026-11-24): B on the cage and the 248 t blanket as an option. The engine still takes 1,575 times its radiator share; the next lever is the source (Q-TH-3).

comparison.title: Edge-on structure and layered blankets together
comparison.why: Together they take 27% of the heat off this engine and cut the 20 K load 19-fold, for 2,208 t per engine. The engine still takes 1,575 times its radiator share, and its windings still need 394 GW of refrigeration.

findings: The 54.6 % is not a geometric quantity. The ledger derives it as (piped heat - hit share x charged power) / neutral power from the compact study: (44.0 TW - 40.5 TW) / 6.38 TW. It is the small difference of two large numbers: one point of hit share moves it by 0.09.
It also comes from a different source state: the steady-plasma spectrum (STEADY, with synchrotron), not the target burn (COUPLED).
The compact study's own sky ledger covered 97.9% of the burn (with the radiator blades and the neighbour engines), and its piped heat leaves out what edge-on fins and the plug re-radiate themselves.

The geometric trace of every drawn part gives 63.1%: shield 7.2%, coils and loops 37.2%, cage, lines and optics 18.6%. The coils, loops and shield alone give 44.4%, close to the ledger figure, which is why the two looked related.
Decision: the COUPLED ledger now uses the geometric trace (63.1 %) for the X-ray and neutron pickup of the compact engine; the old figure is kept and labelled as the compact study's piped share.

residual.finding: The 0.25 % energy residual of the burn was the thermal energy of ions created or lost at fixed temperature (D-D-n and D-T turn two ions into one). The ledger now books it as its own term (number change); about 0.02 % remains, the time-step error of the integration.

tech.physics: more burn-up, but the burning electrons radiate more: the X-ray share grows
tech.enabler: precision target manufacture, pulse shaping by learned controllers

tech.physics: more burn-up at the same yield; a heavy tamper mixes and raises Zeff

tech.physics: an opaque shell turns X-rays into plasma the nozzle can direct; adds exhaust mass

tech.physics: directed 14.7 MeV protons, but the burn loses its self-heating

tech.physics: the products heat electrons first above Ec; Te follows Ti within picoseconds at target density
tech.enabler: none known: the coupling is collisional, not a technology limit

findings: At 70 keV the 14.7 MeV protons give 10% of their energy to ions and the 3.6 MeV alphas 69% (critical energies 0.7 and 3.0 MeV); the rest heats electrons, which radiate. At the design density the products stop within 7.2 um (protons) of a 40 um target, so they all deposit: the target is its own X-ray lamp.
The design burn sends 85% of its fusion energy out as X-rays and leaves 16% as plasma the nozzle can use.
Hot ions at the start change almost nothing (X-ray share 84%): ions and electrons equilibrate in picoseconds at this density. This is a physics limit, not a technology one.
Spin polarisation raises the yield x1.11 and burn-up to 75%, but the X-ray share stays 83%: it helps the fuel, not the radiation.
3He-rich fuel (D:3He 1:3) cuts the neutron share to 0.5% (from 2.9%) at X-ray share 99%.

Early extraction is the only lever that lowers the X-ray share at the source: 20% out gives X-rays 71%, extractable 30%, yield x0.97; 50% out gives X-rays 49%, extractable 53%, yield x0.86; 80% out gives X-rays 41%, extractable 79%, yield x0.18. The burn loses its self-heating, so the yield falls.

A tungsten tamper of 1 g/cm2 round the fuel (3.1% of its mass) would absorb 69% of the X-rays (cold opacity, an upper bound) and leave 44% of the fusion energy as X-rays. The absorbed energy becomes plasma the nozzle can direct, so the exhaust speeds up to 9,062 km/s (0.47 of the mission's) and the impulse per pulse grows x1.90. Light tampers (LiH, carbon) absorb too little.

Density and burn time decide the split: x0.3 areal density gives X-rays 53% and extractable 50% (yield x0.72); a faster disassembly gives 67% and 34%. A denser or longer burn raises burn-up a little and sends almost everything out as X-rays.
The fuel-side levers together (polarised, 3He-rich, tamped, x3 areal density) are the worst case: yield x0.60, X-rays 105% of the fusion energy (the driver heat radiates too).

The source-side levers together (polarised, x0.3 areal density, 20 % early extraction): yield x0.86, burn-up 58%, X-rays 45%, extractable 59%. With a tungsten tamper on top, the X-rays leaving the target fall to 23% of the fusion energy and the thrust grows x2.1, but the engine heat stays x2,011 its radiator share (design x2,200): the plasma that no longer radiates strikes the hardware instead (78% of the heat). The next lever is the nozzle's hit share, not the fuel.
Adding cold propellant lowers the exhaust speed: the design is short of energy per kilogram (coupled exhaust 4,914 km/s against the mission's 19,201 km/s), not short of mass.

states.label: Engine pulse design point
states.source: vertex_engine C-02 (yield at the research armour fluence) and C-04 (rate for 0.25 of the V4 research power per engine): the cluster equals one V4 research drive (35.7 TW, 2.90 MN)

states.source: lab/studies/vertex-compact-engine/vertex-compact at aebbb0d: mission power per engine, fuel source V2 (steady-plasma radiation shares), pulse rate 5,697 Hz taken from the design point, so its implied energy per pulse is not the 1.57 GJ target

burn.note: Shares of the fusion energy from one R2-B target burn. "Left in the plasma" is the energy balance fusion + driver heat - X-rays - neutrons: the thermal and kinetic energy of the expanding charged plasma, the part a nozzle could steer.

encounter.note: per_close_90: fusion against one single hard (90 degree) Coulomb encounter; per_deflection: against the momentum-transfer cross section (many distant small-angle passes, ln Lambda = 20). Both at a fixed pair energy, not a thermal average.

states.label: Mission requirement
states.assumes: operating_point (WORKING): exhaust 19,201 km/s, directed efficiency 0.8, burn-up 0.8 with 95 % of the unburned fuel recovered, hydrogen makes up the rest of the jet. It prescribes the split; it does not model a burn or a nozzle.

states.label: Engine pulse design point
states.assumes: vertex_engine C-02 (yield held at the research armour fluence) and C-04 (rate for 0.25 of the V4 research fusion power): the four engines together are one V4 research drive (35.7 TW, 2.90 MN, converged for a 42,916 t ship). The jet share 0.78 is the research drive's jet power over its fusion power, applied to every yield; the target mass is chosen so that jet leaves at 19,201 km/s.

states.label: Coupled pulse (this ledger)
states.assumes: The design target (mass, areal density, start temperature) and rate, burned by R2-B with every joule and nucleus booked; the nozzle shares of the drawn cluster (C1) from the compact study. Compression and driver coupling are OPEN.
states.source: lab/studies/fusion-ignition/ledger.py (R2-B as vertex_radiation.burn) + lab/studies/vertex-compact-engine/vertex-compact aebbb0d nozzle shares

states.label: Steady-plasma source (losses study)
states.assumes: Vertex 1.6B case S5 optimistic bracket (fuel V2): a steady plasma at n_e 1e+21 m^-3 with Ti 100 keV, 3He 300 keV, Te 46 keV, 54% of the product energy channelled to ions; it does not sustain itself (gain 0.81, auxiliary heating 123% of fusion). The compact study applied these shares at the mission power per engine and the design rate.

reconcile.title: Power: 8.9 TW per engine at the pulse design point, 65.3 TW needed
reconcile.why: The engine was sized (vertex_engine design_power_share 0.25) so that four engines equal one V4 research drive: 35.7 TW and 2.90 MN, converged for a 42,916 t research ship. The mission requirement is the approved 4,426 t ship at 21.8 MN (0.5 g). Neither number is wrong; the drawn engine was never sized for the approved ship. The gap stays OPEN; no coefficient is changed to close it.
reconcile.coupled: With the burn physics coupled (R3) the design point gives 0.74 MN for four engines, not 2.90 MN. To give the mission thrust with this target each engine would fire 167,429 times a second (262 TW of fusion per engine) and the exhaust would leave at 4,914 km/s instead of 19,201 km/s; the engine would take up 64,646 times its radiator share.

reconcile.title: X-rays: 85 % of the energy in the target burn, 6.3 % in the losses stage
reconcile.verdict: EXPLAINED: different plasmas; the losses stage used the wrong regime for a pulsed target
reconcile.why: The 6.3 % is the instantaneous bremsstrahlung of a steady plasma at n_e 1e+21 m^-3 held at Te 46 keV while the ions run at 100-300 keV, with 54% of the product energy channelled to ions and auxiliary heating of 123% of the fusion power (not self-sustaining). In the target (n_e about 9e+33 m^-3) nothing channels or removes the product energy: 63% of it goes straight to the electrons, which reach 247 keV (ions 630 keV). At that temperature bremsstrahlung, with its relativistic terms, is 27% of the fusion power at the start, 83% when half the yield is made and 127% at 90 %: as the fuel burns out and the target expands, the heat the electrons hold radiates faster than new fusion replaces it. The 85 % is that energy integrated over the burn. The two are different regimes; neither is tuned.
reconcile.coupled: The coupled ledger uses the target burn for the pulsed engine. The losses stage now shows the coupled X-rays and keeps the steady-plasma figure as a separate, labelled regime.

reconcile.title: Charged energy: 78 % assumed by the engine, 17 % left in the plasma
reconcile.verdict: INCONSISTENT: the design point assumes more jet than its own burn leaves
reconcile.why: The 0.78 is not a charged-product share: it is the V4 research drive's jet power over its fusion power (27.86 / 35.72 TW), applied to every pulse, and it sets the target mass (6.6 mg) and the 19,201 km/s exhaust. At birth 97.1% of the fusion energy is charged (only D-D side reactions make neutrons). But the products cannot leave a target this dense: they heat it, the electrons radiate, and when the burn ends 16.4% of the fusion energy is still plasma energy that a nozzle could use. The burn that makes the design yield cannot also deliver the design jet.
reconcile.coupled: Plasma 16.4% of fusion x nozzle 0.31 (C1) = 5.1% jet; the exhaust leaves at 4,914 km/s and the design pulse gives 26% of the design thrust.

reconcile.title: Fuel masses: injected or reacted
reconcile.why: Mission (operating_point.species): the D and 3He tonnes are REACTED fuel; the tanks feed 1.25 times that (burn-up 0.8) and get 95% of the unburned part back. The unrecovered feed, 1.25% of the reacted mass, leaves in the jet but is counted in the hydrogen line, so the 3He and D lines understate the fuel the tanks lose by that much (a bookkeeping note for the owner, not changed here). Engine pulse: the old fuel stage showed the reacted D and 3He (4.45 mg, from the yield and the D-3He energy alone) as "per pulse"; the injected target is 6.63 mg. Its "burned share 67%" is that ratio, and the burn agrees: it consumes 67% of the injected fuel by mass. The ignition stage's "burn fraction 77%" is the share of the deuterium used (D-D side reactions use two deuterons and little energy), so it is now labelled as such. A pulsed target has no recovery: its unburned fuel leaves with the exhaust. The fuel stage also divided the mission hydrogen flow by the design pulse rate, mixing two states; the coupled ledger adds no hydrogen, because no model says how it would be heated.
reconcile.coupled: The ledger books per pulse: injected 6.63 mg, reacted 4.48 mg (67%), mass turned into energy 0.0174 mg, exhaust 6.61 mg.

timeline.title: Target flight to the burn point
timeline.note: One target in flight per period (vertex_engine C-08); launcher and tracking are VTX-S2.

timeline.title: Compression and heating
timeline.note: Not modelled: the burn starts from a compressed sphere holding 67 MJ of heat. The driver must put at least that into the fuel; its coupling efficiency is OPEN.

timeline.title: Burn
timeline.note: R2-B with the full ledger (history below).

timeline.title: Plasma to the nozzle exit
timeline.note: The plasma leaves at about 8,810 km/s (its energy over its mass) and crosses the 12.4 m to the exit; the nozzle shares are IMPORTED test-particle results, so how the energy turns inside the nozzle is not resolved in time.

limits: Compression and driver coupling are not modelled (OPEN): the driver figures are lower bounds at full coupling and 50% wall-plug efficiency (ignition-failures assumption).
Nozzle shares are IMPORTED from test particles at birth energies and burn-debris speed in the vacuum field; the expanding plasma's own response (detachment, collective effects) is not modelled.
Every fusion product deposits its energy inside the target (R2-B deposition 1.0); the reactivity is held at the Bosch-Hale fit limit (190 keV) where the ions run hotter.
X-rays escape the target freely (R2-B: Compton depth 0.1-1 only downshifts them).
Hydrogen propellant coupling is not modelled; with hydrogen the ledger returns no thrust.
The steady-plasma levers (polarisation, hot-ion mode, 3He heating) belong to the steady regime and are not coupled to the target burn.
